title: Kebab soltani
subtitle: Persian mixed lamb skewers with saffron
excerpt: Kebab soltani is the royal Persian combination: one skewer of flat lamb fillet (barg) and one of minced lamb koobideh on the same plate, both marinated with saffron and served over chelow with grilled tomatoes and butter. Soltani means sultan's, reflecting the elevated status of the dish.
sourceNotes: Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life: Ancient Persian and Modern Iranian Cooking and Ceremonies (1986). Kebab soltani documented as the combination platter of Iranian kebab culture. Margaret Shaida, The Legendary Cuisine of Persia (1992). Notes on the chelo kabab tradition and the barg and koobideh pairing.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the barg overnight. Prepare the koobideh mix the same day and refrigerate for 30 minutes before grilling.
recipe.temperatureNote: Grill or griddle at the highest heat possible.

content.text: Kebab soltani is the combination of two Persian kebabs on one plate: a skewer of barg (flat marinated lamb fillet) and a skewer of koobideh (minced lamb), both marinated with saffron and grilled over high heat. The name means the sultan's kebab, and it is what you order at an Iranian kebab restaurant to get the best of both. Served with chelow, grilled tomatoes, fresh herbs, and a pat of butter on the hot rice.

items.prepNote: boneless, cut into thin flat fillets for the barg
ground, dissolved in 3 tbsp hot water, cooled
to dot over the hot rice and kebabs

content.text: Mix the cooled dissolved {{saffron}}, half the squeezed {{onion}}, half the {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}}, lemon juice from {{lemon}}, half the {{sea-salt-fine}}, and half the {{black-pepper}} together. Add the {{lamb-leg}} fillets, coat well, and refrigerate for at least four hours.

Combine {{lamb-mince}} with the remaining squeezed {{onion}}, 2 tablespoons of the saffron marinade, the remaining {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{black-pepper}}. Knead firmly for three minutes until sticky and cohesive. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Thread the barg fillets onto flat metal skewers in a zigzag pattern. Mould the koobideh mixture around separate flat skewers in sausage shapes about 15 cm long.

Preheat a griddle pan or grill to the highest heat. Grill the barg for three to four minutes per side and the koobideh for four to five minutes per side, turning once. Add the halved {{tomato}} alongside to grill. Rest for five minutes.
Plate over chelow with the grilled {{tomato}}. Dot {{unsalted-butter}} over the hot rice and scatter {{sumac}} on top.

items.symptom: The koobideh is falling off the skewer
items.cause: Not kneaded enough or too much onion liquid
items.fix: Knead until the mixture is very sticky and passes the squeeze test. Squeeze all liquid from the onion before adding.
Barg fillets should be at least 1 cm thick. Three to four minutes per side on high heat is enough.

items.symptom: The saffron flavour doesn't come through
items.cause: Saffron added to cold water rather than hot
items.fix: Always dissolve saffron in near-boiling water and let it steep for five minutes. The colour should be a deep burnt orange.

items.symptom: The koobideh is dense and heavy
items.fix: Fat is essential in koobideh. Use lamb mince with at least 20% fat; ask your butcher if unsure.

content.text: Chelo kabab (rice with kebab) is the closest thing Iran has to a national dish. Every city has its kebab restaurants; every family has opinions about who makes the best. The soltani combination (one barg, one koobideh) is the definitive order. The dish comes to the table with a mountain of saffron-tinted chelow rice with a raw egg yolk on top (mixed in at the table), a whole grilled tomato, a pat of butter, and a small pile of sumac. The meal is assembled at the table: butter melted into the rice, tomato squeezed over, sumac scattered. It is one of the most complete dining experiences in Persian cuisine.
